A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoCogNav and the CEN dataset. All pages, equations, tables, and figures are readable and matchable across versions. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports original trajectory, head-motion, and perceived-uncertainty prediction experiments, including baseline comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds modality-ablation results in Table 4 and uncertainty-label validation results in Section 4.2.

M1.justification: The late-fusion architecture, uncertainty head, learnable memory, uncertainty-conditioned decoding, and training losses remain unchanged. Specifying the DINOv2 CLS token adds implementation detail without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same reported CEN coverage: six hours, 17 participants, 226k frames, and 42 indoor/outdoor sites, with the same forecasting tasks. V3 removes MULT from the environment-annotation list but does not report removing recordings or changing the evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Const_Vel, Lin_Ext, M_Transformer, and adapted EgoCast; Table 2 retains EMU and PATH_U. V3 clarifies that EgoCast uses the same frozen DINOv2 features, without establishing a revised comparator implementation.

E3.justification: Section 5 replaces the stated test setting of environments unseen during training with held-out traversal instances, head/gaze movements, and local observations along shared waypoint sequences. This substantially revises the reported generalization protocol, without establishing that the partition changed or experiments were rerun. Table 4 also introduces modality-removal controls.

E4.justification: V3 adds a focused modality ablation testing motion, goal, video, head history, and gaze. Section 4.2 adds validation of self-reported uncertainty against environment categories and independently annotated behaviors. Existing component ablations, behavior-specific analyses, qualitative examples, and failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 newly reports standardized behavioral effect sizes: Cohen's d of 0.80 for wrong turns, 0.66 for look-backs, and 0.55 for backtracking. Neither version reports training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical scores in Tables 1–3 and v2 Table 4/v3 Table 5 are unchanged. New Table 4 reports modality variants: Motion Only ADE/FDE is 0.156/0.314 versus Full 0.105/0.207, but Full uncertainty MAE of 0.0986 is worse than +Video's 0.0968. Section 4.2 adds environment proportions, uncertainty means, and behavioral effect sizes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same mathematical operations and objectives. V3 explains the existing goal coordinates and temporal standard-deviation term; it introduces no new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion withdraw the claim of generalization to unseen environments and instead claim improved forecasting on held-out navigation recordings. This materially narrows a headline empirical claim, while retaining the joint forecasting task, EgoCogNav architecture, and CEN dataset contributions.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the new annotation statistics as evidence that joystick uncertainty reflects navigation difficulty, makes the gradient-coupling explanation more cautious, and narrows the interpretation of generalization. Section 5.3 adds specific dataset limitations concerning participant, scene, route, and annotation diversity.

D1.justification: V3 specifies CLS-token visual features and the shared frozen DINOv2 backbone for adapted EgoCast, discloses two independent behavior annotators and IRB approval, and adds a project-page link. Hardware and training hyperparameters remain unchanged; the link alone does not establish code or data availability.

R1.justification: The same 73 references and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Section 2 receives grammatical edits without changing its comparison to prior trajectory, uncertainty, memory, or egocentric-dataset research.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized grammatical corrections, updates an author affiliation, expands several explanations, and revises the ablation discussion and conclusion. The section hierarchy and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds the modality-ablation table as Table 4 and renumbers the existing behavior table to Table 5. Tables and surrounding text are redistributed across pages. All four figure images and their captions are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 better calibrates its generalization claims to the described evaluation and adds useful modality and uncertainty-label validation, alongside clearer implementation disclosures. These improve support and transparency without changing the core method or existing scores. The gains remain limited: exact split construction is still unspecified, and the new modality table shows tradeoffs across metrics.
